sentence: This project tries to find out which human cell proteins affect how bacteria grow inside cells, using a standard laboratory microscope to perform DNA sequencing.
This project tests whether a protein drives hepatocellular carcinoma and can be a target for treatment, using humanized mice and CRISPR screening.
This project develops biodegradable nerve guidance conduits that are epigenetically stimulating and photoacoustic to repair peripheral nerve defects.
This project builds software and next generation sequencing analysis pipelines for viral research in computational biology.
This project develops light-activated metal compounds as tools for biomedical imaging and photo-control.
This project studies where an mRNA goes and which proteins it interacts with as neurons remodel their axons and dendrites in fruit fly models.
This project investigates how an injectable biomaterials-based vaccine system improves host immunity against Staphylococcus aureus joint infection in murine and rabbit models.
This project tries to understand how proteins that change the structure of RNA and DNA work, and why defects in them lead to diseases.
This project uses large-scale genetic studies, electronic health records and machine learning to build predictive models for psychiatry.
This project studies how the spatial organization of the human genome relates to brain development and how its disruption might lead to neurodevelopmental disorders.
This project profiles human genes, proteins, and metabolites using omics profiling technologies.
This project studies how an abnormal molecule disrupts the formation of blood cells and causes a form of leukemia in newborns and toddlers.
This project develops a technology for amplifying single-stranded DNA molecules efficiently and uniformly.
This project builds software that uses deep learning to outline key brain structures and predict how radiation changes them in children with brain tumors.
This project carries out a molecular genetics study of bipolar disorder using whole genome sequence and phenotype data.
This project uses electron microscopy to look at protein-DNA structures and protein-protein shapes of herpesviruses that cause human cancers.
This project studies how T cells can be made to attack acute myeloid leukemia in humanized mouse models.
This project offers tools that analyze complex cancer phenotypes within tumors in a spatially resolved manner.
This project develops a dual-targeting nanotherapeutic to overcome resistance to targeted therapies in cancers.
This project studies how a sensory neuron receptor and its human version contribute to chronic itch.
